red_flags.title: Empty project dossier — no capacity, acreage, or facts to underwrite
red_flags.evidence: Project record lists capacity 0.0 MW, site acres null, and zero extracted facts. No CEQA class, no Opt-In eligibility (needs ≥50 MW solar + ≥200 MWh storage), no COD, no BOC, no interconnection, no financials. Cannot establish statutory path, tax-credit eligibility, or economic viability.
red_flags.benchmark: Opt-In eligibility: solar ≥50 MW, storage ≥200 MWh

red_flags.title: ITC/PTC cliff deadline already passed — BOC evidence unverified
red_flags.evidence: Under OBBBA, a solar project with COD after 2029 forfeits the 30% ITC unless physical-work beginning-of-construction was documented by July 4, 2026 — a deadline that has already passed. The dossier provides no BOC evidence, no COD, and no capacity. This is the single largest go/no-go item.
red_flags.benchmark: BOC documented by Jul 4, 2026 (Notice 2025-42); continuity safe harbor → PIS by Dec 31, 2030
sources: kb_lookup: ITC cliff — deadline already passed (OBBBA/Notice 2025-42)

red_flags.title: Likely federal land / gen-tie crossing → NEPA + ROW, multi-year
red_flags.evidence: Trinity County is dominated by Shasta-Trinity National Forest and Trinity Alps Wilderness. Any gen-tie crossing federal land requires a BLM ROW grant, NEPA review, and plan conformance — precedent runs 2–3 years and is appeal-prone. Parcel ownership and gen-tie route are unverified.
red_flags.benchmark: BLM NEPA ~2–3 years; ROW grant + plan conformance required for federal crossings
sources: kb_lookup: BLM 2024 Western Solar Plan ROD; Townsite Solar 2 precedent

red_flags.title: Timberland Conversion Permit likely required (forested parcel)
red_flags.evidence: Trinity County is heavily forested. Converting timberland to solar requires a Timberland Conversion Permit under the Z'berg-Nejedly Forest Practice Act — a distinct, lengthy, and often-contested approval not present in the dossier. Parcel vegetation/land-use class is unverified.
red_flags.benchmark: Forest Practice Act TCR required for timberland conversion

red_flags.title: Zoning district unverified — potential solar prohibition in rural/forestry districts
red_flags.evidence: Trinity County's zoning for parcel 025-340-12-00 could not be confirmed (county planning/assessor pages returned 404). Rural forested counties commonly restrict or prohibit commercial solar in timber/agriculture districts. If prohibited, the only viable path is CEC Opt-In (≥50 MW + ≥200 MWh), which preempts local zoning.
red_flags.benchmark: Local route 18–36 months with denial risk; Opt-In 270-day CEC clock
sources: kb_lookup: zoning kill-switch pattern; CEC Opt-In preempts local zoning

red_flags.title: Northern spotted owl / Trinity River fish habitat — ESA risk unassessed
red_flags.evidence: Trinity County is core northern spotted owl and Trinity River anadromous-fish habitat. Forest conversion and stream crossings would require ESA/CESA consultation and seasonal survey windows; no biological surveys, no AB 52 tribal consultation, and no Sacred Lands search are in the dossier.
red_flags.benchmark: ESA-listed species presence drives survey windows; miss a season = +1 year; AB 52 consultation must conclude before EIR certification
sources: kb_lookup: species protocols drive schedule (miss a window = +1 year)

red_flags.title: Weak rural northern-CA transmission — interconnection is the critical path
red_flags.evidence: Trinity County is in PG&E/CAISO territory with weak rural transmission. CAISO queue is >500 GW with only ~20% reaching COD; PG&E deprioritized projects average +8.4 years delay. No queue position, POI, or study is documented. For any near-term COD, a cluster study must complete ~mid-2027.
red_flags.benchmark: IR→COD ~5 years; PG&E deprioritized projects +8.4 years; only ~20% of queued projects reach COD
sources: kb_lookup: CAISO queue reality; PG&E deprioritized projects +8.4 years

red_flags.title: Poor solar resource for far-northern mountainous site
red_flags.evidence: Trinity County's far-northern latitude, mountainous terrain, and forest cover yield materially lower GHI than the Central Valley (Solano ~5.32 kWh/m²/day) or desert sites (5.8–6.2). Lower capacity factor and steep-slope siting reduce energy yield and raise cost per MWh. No irradiance study is in the dossier.
red_flags.benchmark: GHI 5.8–6.2 kWh/m²/day (desert); Solano 5.32; Trinity expected well below
sources: kb_lookup: resource benchmarks (Copper Mountain 4 CF 32.3%; Solano GHI 5.32)

red_flags.title: Transformer/GSU lead time 128–144 weeks — order window missed for near-term COD
red_flags.evidence: 2025–26 market norm for large power transformers/GSUs is 128–144 weeks (~2.5–2.8 years). For any 2028–2029 COD, orders had to be placed by mid-2025. No equipment procurement plan is documented.
sources: kb_lookup: transformers worse than demo — 128–144 weeks

red_flags.title: No offtake/PPA — projects without PPAs nearly always withdraw from CAISO queue
red_flags.evidence: Trinity County has no CCA (PG&E territory). Offtake requires PG&E IRP/CPUC procurement or a bilateral PPA. CAISO TPD allocation prioritizes executed PPAs — projects without PPAs nearly always withdraw. No offtake strategy is documented.
red_flags.benchmark: Executed PPA first for TPD allocation; projects without PPAs nearly always withdraw
sources: kb_lookup: CAISO TPD allocation priority; no CCAs in PG&E territory

red_flags.title: No financial model — CAPEX, escalation, and revenue unverifiable
red_flags.evidence: No CAPEX, $/W, escalation reserve, or revenue model is provided. Real benchmark is $1.43–1.56/Wac installed (LBNL/NREL); any figure near half of market is a red flag. Merchant tails must be underwritten to 2025 benchmarks ($52/kW-yr battery revenue), not 2022 vintage.
sources: kb_lookup: CAPEX confirmed impossible at $0.74/W; merchant revenue compression

red_flags.title: Rural community opposition and limited local infrastructure
red_flags.evidence: Trinity County is a small, economically depressed, forested county with no established utility-scale solar land-use pattern. Large industrial solar on forested land is likely to draw local opposition; the county lacks the staff and grid infrastructure to support a large project. No community engagement or CBA is documented.
red_flags.benchmark: CBA anchors $0.5–5M one-time; treat <$1,000/MW as below-market
sources: kb_lookup: community/CBA benchmarks; rural ag siting opposition
